title: Ansel and the Terminal
premise: Navigator Lena Eriksen ferries cargo along a route of worlds that severed contact after a diplomatic collapse, haunted by the frozen backups of dead crewmates she was ordered to abandon in her hold. When the survey ship Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew aged backward and its logs wiped, Lena discovers the 'impossible' voyage hides a massacre on the colony world Vesper Gate — one the Concord's records now insist never happened. Partnering with Ansel, a Halcyon survivor whose reversed memories surface in fragments, she races to recover the erased truth while Concord enforcers close in. In the end Lena broadcasts the raw evidence from the backups in her own hold, sacrificing her ship and her clean record, and chooses Ansel — and justice outside the law — over the duty that once made her complicit.
about_author: Odile Oyelaran is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town in Norway, where the long silences between transmissions taught her how much of a story lives in what goes unsaid.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet Route
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She runs cargo between silent worlds, performing maintenance on the backup pods in her hold she's forbidden to open. Establishes her guilt and the Concord's chokehold on communication. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as professionalism.

chapters.title: Signal from Nowhere
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A derelict transponder pings from empty space: the Halcyon, missing eleven years, returning. She diverts against protocol, first act of disobedience. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: Everyone Younger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She boards the Halcyon and finds the crew biologically reversed — adults now children, the captain an old man made young. One survivor, Ansel, is intact but remembers nothing. Emotional beat: uncanny dread mixed with tenderness.

chapters.title: Ansel
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, fragmented and disoriented. He wakes among reversed crewmates, clutching a data shard he doesn't remember taking. He trusts Lena instantly and doesn't know why. Emotional beat: trust as instinct, memory as wound.

chapters.title: The Concord Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Concord Inspector Veyr impounds the Halcyon and declares the crew's condition a navigation accident. Lena notices the logs were rewritten with her own shipping code — someone framed her. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Shard Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The shard plays back fragments: a colony, Vesper Gate, screaming, then silence. Ansel begins aging forward rapidly as his timeline corrects, gaining memories as he loses years. Emotional beat: grief arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: Duty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Veyr offers Lena amnesty if she surrenders the shard and the Halcyon crew. She calculates the cost of defiance and finds she's already spent too much to stop. Emotional beat: the moment duty stops being enough.

chapters.title: The Hold
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She finally opens the forbidden backup pods and finds the dead crewmates' final recordings — including evidence of the Vesper Gate evacuation order she once relayed. Emotional beat: shame confronted, complicity named.

chapters.title: Running the Silent Worlds
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lena and Ansel flee with the shard, hopping worlds that cut contact years ago, finding allies among smugglers and exiles. Emotional beat: fugitive freedom, love kindling under pressure.

chapters.title: Vesper Gate, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They reach Vesper Gate's ruins: a colony that officially never existed. Ansel's memories complete — the Halcyon witnessed the Concord's purge and fled through a time-dilation fold, which reversed them. Emotional beat: horror made physical.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Veyr's enforcers arrive; the reversed crew are taken as 'evidence.' Lena realizes the Concord isn't hiding the massacre — it's hiding that the victims' backups still exist somewhere. Emotional beat: rage at bureaucratic erasure.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel bargains with a Concord archivist, Ilsa, who kept illegal copies of suppressed records out of private conscience. She confirms the victims' backups are stored at the Meridian Vault. Emotional beat: hope found in an unlikely defector.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Ansel, now aging past his true years, begins forgetting Lena as his mind races forward. He urges her to finish without him. Emotional beat: love against the clock, duty to the mission over the self.

chapters.title: The Meridian Vault
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Infiltration of the Concord's memory archive. They find the Vesper Gate backups intact — thousands of witnesses the law says don't exist. Emotional beat: awe and terror in the cathedral of stolen memories.

chapters.title: Veyr's Truth
chapters.summary: Veyr's POV. The inspector confronts them, revealing she knows everything and has been ordered to bury it — and that her own family is among the backups. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as another captive of duty.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Veyr hesitates; enforcer reinforcements don't. Ilsa dies buying them time to escape with a backup core. Ansel collapses, his accelerated aging critical. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the price of choosing sides.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena rigs her own ship's long-range array to transmit the backups' testimony to every silent world at once — the act that once made her complicit now reversed. Emotional beat: redemption through the same instrument of her guilt.

chapters.title: The Worlds Answer
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across the route, silent worlds light up with replies; the Concord's record collapses under a chorus of living witnesses. Enforcers stand down as Veyr testifies. Emotional beat: the long silence breaking.

chapters.title: Ansel's Hour
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Dying of timeline collapse, Ansel is given a choice: restoration from his own backup — becoming a copy — or ending as himself. He asks Lena what love owes to continuity. Emotional beat: the book's central question made intimate.

chapters.title: The Man Who Came Back Twice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Ansel chooses restoration. The man who wakes remembers everything, including her — but knows he is not quite the same man. Lena chooses him anyway. Emotional beat: love that survives the loss of permanence.

chapters.title: Hearings and After
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Concord convenes a tribunal; Lena refuses amnesty, insisting on public accountability for her own relayed order. Vesper Gate's survivors are restored from backup and given voice. Emotional beat: justice as process, not verdict.

chapters.title: The Route Reopened
chapters.summary: Lena and Ansel's alternating POV, closing. They take a new ship down a route where worlds speak again, the hold empty of ghosts at last. Lena transmits one final log: the truth, kept. Emotional beat: peace earned, silence ended.
